newsitem.title: USA: BOXING-CHAVEZ STILL HAS PLENTY OF FIGHT LEFT IN HIM SAYS MARTIN.
newsitem.headline: BOXING-CHAVEZ STILL HAS PLENTY OF FIGHT LEFT IN HIM SAYS MARTIN.

text.p: Julio Cesar Chavez still has a lot of fight left in him says Tony Martin, who clashes with the ageing superstar on Saturday.
"I think he still brings a lot (to the ring)," Martin said of the 34-year-old Chavez, a former six-time champion at a new conference earlier this week at the Las Vegas Hilton.
"He is always dangerous," Martin said of Chavez, 98-2-1, 83KOs. "He is a hell of a body puncher, he is strong, and gutsy."
Chavez dominated the middle weight divisions for years, holding world titles in the super lightweight,junior welterweight, lightweight and super featherweight divisions.
"He is a legend, no doubt. I can't take anything from him," Martin said.

Chavez and Martin, 34-5-1, meet in a scheduled 10-round non-title junior welterweight bout in the card for Michael Moorer's defence of his International Boxing Federation heavyweight crown against fellow American Vaughn Bean.
Moorer, 38-1, is a 6-to-1 betting favourite to beat the more inexperienced number five rated contender Bean, 27-0, 21 KOs.
"I'm on a totally different level," Moorer has said of Bean. "He has to step up to my level, which he has never done before and I'm going to put him right back down to the level where he belongs."
Chavez certainly belongs in the Hall of Fame when he retires. He is idolised by his countrymen, having once drawn a record 136,000 fans to watch him fight in Mexico City in 1993.
ButChavez has begun to show signs of slipping. He was badly bloodied and beaten by Oscar de la Hoya in four rounds to lose his World Boxing Council super lightweight title last June.
But instead of letting that defeat discourage him, Chavez has used it to motivate him to become a champion again.

"A lot of negative things have been said about me being too old and over the hill," said Chavez, who is a 3-to-1 betting favourite against Martin. "This Saturday everybody will be able to judge if I still have it.
"God willing, I will be fighting for the title again. I will be champion again," Chavez said.
Martin is not surprised by Chavez's resiliency.

"He is one of those guys who has to be convinced that he lost," said Martin, 36, who has won his last four fights. "He still doesn't know how to lose and that is my job, to convince him that he is losing.
"He is a guy who you just have to beat,"said Martin.
